data.title: Altair at 50: Remembering the first Personal Computer
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 《Altair at 50: 纪念第一台个人电脑》一文回顾了1975年由MITS公司推出的Altair 8800，这台电脑被认为是首台商用成功的个人电脑，比苹果和Commodore的电脑更早。Altair基于Intel 8080 CPU，通过《Popular Electronics》杂志宣传，以397美元的套件形式出售，用户需自行组装，初期仅有256字节RAM，无键盘和显示器，通过开关和指示灯操作。尽管初期计划售出200套以达到收支平衡，但最终卖出了约25,000套，激发了比尔·盖茨和保罗·艾伦为其开发BASIC语言，进而促成了微软的成立。Altair还启发了史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克设计第一台苹果电脑，并引入了S-100总线，对后续计算机产生深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Altair 8800电脑的历史、影响、及其相关技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• **关于Altair 8800的模拟器**：musicale列举了多个Altair 8800的模拟器链接，指出可以在这些模拟器上运行CP/M系统，但也提到其使用上不如其他CP/M模拟器方便。
• **对Ed Roberts的个人生平的关注**：NoSalt对Altair 8800的发明者Ed Roberts的生平做了详细描述，强调了他多重职业背景和成就。
• **对历史杂志内容的兴趣**：shakna被评论中的杂志封面吸引，提到杂志中关于计算器组装的详细步骤，并提供了相关链接。
• **个人经历与历史设备**：embedded_hiker分享了自己在学校期间通过 teletype 和HP2000C学习编程的经历。CarVac提到自己拥有IMSAI 8080设备，并讲述了其教授不建议他从事计算机职业的故事。
• **Altair 8800的价格与复刻版**：danbruc对比了Altair 8800当年的价格和如今在eBay上的售价，并提到现在有售价150美元的迷你复刻版。
• **其他早期计算机的提及**：jodydonetti提到Olivetti P101（1965），oldnetguy则认为Kenbak 1才是第一台个人计算机，dcassett补充了Mark-8这个早期的"套件计算机"。

补充讨论：
• **对微软诞生历史的影响**：igtztorrero强调了Altair 8800对微软创立的重要影响，提到比尔·盖茨和保罗·艾伦如何在Altair 8800上开发BASIC语言，并促成了微软的诞生。
• **个人捐赠经历**：vondur提到自己从岳父那里得到了Altair 8800并捐赠给了当地大学。
• **对早期PC的认知**：berlinbrowndev表示自己原以为TRS和Commodore 64才是最早的个人电脑，显示出对Altair 8800作为早期PC代表的不了解。

争议焦点：
• **最早的个人计算机之争**：在提到Altair 8800时，有人认为它是第一台个人计算机，但oldnetguy提出Kenbak 1更早，而dcassett则补充了Mark-8这个早期的"套件计算机"，显示出对"第一台个人计算机"定义的不同看法。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Altair 8800的历史地位、技术细节、相关模拟器及其对个人计算机历史的影响展开讨论，同时掺杂了一些个人经历和相关早期计算机的提及。

You might think that Apple, Commodore or perhaps Radio Shack made the first personal computer, but you’d be wrong. Although the Apple I appeared in 1976, and then in 1977 the Apple II, Commodore PET and TRS-80 all appeared, there was one personal computer that preceded them all: The MITS Altair 8800 from 1975, considered the first commercially successful personal computer.
The Altair was created by a small company called MITS, which initially stood for Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry. In 1974 MITS had been selling calculator kits via mail order. Later in the year they started working on a computer based on the then-new
Intel 8080 8-bit CPU
. About this time they were contacted by Popular Electronics magazine who was looking to do a feature on a computer project.
The Altair name was taken from the brightest star in the Aquila constellation. It is one of the closest stars to Earth and the name was considered futuristic.
This all coincided with the January 1975 issue of Popular Electronics. The Altair
1
was featured on the cover and there was a companion article (written by Ed Roberts, owner of MITS) titled “Project Breakthrough! World’s First Mini-computer Kit to Rival Commercial Models”.
The computer kit sold for $397 (about $2359 in 2023). Being a kit, that meant that you had to assemble the computer yourself. It didn’t even have a keyboard or display as you used it via its toggle switches and blinking lights!
If you love retro computing, please consider subscribing to Goto 10. Thanks!
Subscribe
For your money you got the case, power supply, motherboard, CPU board, front panel with switches and LEDs, 256 bytes of RAM and assembly instructions. You could pay a little more and have it pre-assembled for you, but that would have delayed delivery. It was so popular that people were known to drive to Albuquerque, New Mexico to personally pick one up!
The Altair doesn’t look all that “personal” today, but it is considered a personal computer because a single person could afford to purchase it themselves, something remarkable for 1975.
Initially MITS had hoped to sell about 200 kits in order to break even, but they sold many, many more than that. Estimates are that about 1,000 were sold in the first month and that about 25,000 kits were sold in total. The percentage of those kits that were successfully assembled by customers is likely pretty low, however. I suspect many people wanted (and bought) one just so they could say they had a computer!
Jan 1975 Popular Electronics
11.6MB ∙ PDF file
Download
Download
The Popular Science article caught the eyes of Bill Gates and Paul Allen. Bill was a student at Harvard at the time and he knew Paul from when they both attended Lakeside School in Seattle. They decided they needed to jump on this new industry that was forming before their eyes and worked quickly on a version of BASIC for the Altair.
This BASIC was implemented on the Harvard PDP-10 mainframes by Bill and others (using an emulator they also had to write since they didn’t have an actual Altair to use), with Paul Allen flying to Albuquerque New Mexico in the summer to demonstrate it to Ed Roberts.
There were some ethical questions regarding the use of the Harvard computers to development commercial software. I believe Harvard put some rules in place to prevent this from happening again.
A deal was made and Microsoft (or Micro Soft as it was at the beginning) was formed. BASIC gave the Altair an actual useful program and made it easier for people to write their own programs, although you needed to also upgrade the Altair to at least 4K of RAM ($$$) to even run it.
On April 2 2025, the 50th anniversary of Altair BASIC,
Bill Gates made the original assembly source code available in the form of a PDF
. Others have since put it on
GitHub in text format
.
A snippet of the Altair BASIC assembly source code
The Altair didn’t survive for very long, but essentially being responsible for the creation of Microsoft is a pretty Big Deal. It also inspired a young Steve Wozniak to create the first Apple computer, using the less expensive MOS 6502 CPU. This first Apple I was also primarily a kit.
The Altair also introduced the S-100 bus that became a standard that was used in a variety of other niche computers around the late 70s.
I was able to see an Altair 8800 when I visited the London Science Museum a couple years ago. It was somewhat larger than I expected.
Altair 8800b computer with a photo of Ed Roberts and the January 1975 issue of Popular Science that kicked off the personal computer industry.
Here is the text from the placard:
Altair 8800b personal co

data.title: Converting a Git repo from tabs to spaces (2016)
data.author: keybored
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者如何将Yelp的主要Python代码库从使用制表符（tabs）转换为空格（spaces）的过程。由于Python生态系统普遍遵循四个空格的缩进方式，而Yelp的代码一直使用制表符，这给开发人员带来了一些困扰。在2013年底，作者决定将整个代码库从制表符转换为四个空格。文章详细介绍了转换前的准备工作，如确保不改变主意、修复不一致的缩进，以及使用Git过滤器防止新制表符进入代码库。作者还提供了具体的技术步骤和建议，如使用`compileall`模块查找缩进错误，并建议在所有人都停止工作时进行这种大规模更改，以减少冲突。文章最后强调，作者不再关心制表符与空格的争论，且无法再逆转当年的更改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Git 中处理大规模机械性变更（如格式化、制表符与空格转换）的最佳实践及其对 `git blame` 等工具的影响

不同观点：
• mmastrac 认为 Git 应该引入一种机制，允许某些提交被标记为 "blame-free"，以避免机械性变更影响 `git blame` 的使用。他后来提到 `.git-blame-ignore-revs` 可以解决部分问题。
• rurban 则表示不需要复杂的解决方案，只需通过简单的命令执行大规模格式化变更，并认为不需要使用 `.gitattribute` 过滤器或“魔法重写”，直接提交即可。
• joshstrange 支持 mmastrac 的观点，认为大规模机械性变更会“污染” `git blame`，并且在 IDE 中查看变更历史时会感到不便，强调了 `.git-blame-ignore-revs` 的重要性。他还提到了团队中有人对破坏 `git blame` 的担忧。
• Alifatisk 对为什么要将制表符转换为空格表示不解，质疑这种操作的必要性。
• gwbas1c 提供了在 .net 生态系统中通过 `.editorconfig` 文件控制格式的方法，并建议在 GitHub Actions 中使用该配置文件以确保代码风格一致。
• zzo38computer 指出某些文件（如 Gopher 菜单和 Makefile）需要保留制表符，说明并非所有情况下都适合将制表符转换为空格。
• s09dfhks 对其他人提到的“拟人化”或“吉祥物”提交方式表示困惑和不满。
• baobun 提供了另一种使用 `find` 和 `sed` 命令处理制表符转换的简化方法。
• gwbas1c 还分享了一个因将制表符替换为空格导致测试失败的趣闻，强调了在代码中使用可见字符的重要性。
• kgwxd 对程序员普遍喜欢固定宽度字体但同时对某些字符（如制表符）有不同偏好表示不解。
• user9999999999 强烈支持使用分号作为块范围标识符，反对使用空白字符（如制表符和空格）来定义代码块。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应允许机械性变更提交影响 `git blame`，部分人（如 mmastrac、joshstrange）认为应有机制避免这种影响，而 rurban 则认为无需复杂解决方案。
• 制表符与空格的优劣和使用场景也是一个讨论点，部分人（如 Alifatisk、zzo38computer）质疑或指出某些情况下制表符不应被转换为空格。
• 工具和自动化的使用，如 `.editorconfig` 和 CI 规则，被建议作为确保代码格式一致性的有效手段（gwbas1c）。
• 关于代码风格的个人偏好，如固定宽度字体和不同字符的使用，引发了对程序员习惯的讨论（kgwxd、user9999999999）。

43869236.article_content:
This post is about the thing in the title.
I used to work for Yelp.  For historical reasons — probably “the initial developers preferred it” — their mostly-Python codebase had always been indented with tabs.  That’s in stark contrast to the vast majority of the Python ecosystem, which generally uses the
standard library’s style guide
recommendation of four spaces.  The presence of tabs caused occasional minor headaches and grumbles among the Python developers, who now numbered in the dozens and were generally used to spaces.
At the end of 2013, I bestowed Yelp with a Christmas gift: I converted their
entire primary codebase
from tabs to four spaces.  On the off chance anyone else ever wants to do the same, here’s how I did it.  Probably.  I mean, it’s been two and a half years, but I wrote most of this at the time, so it should be correct.
Please note: I
do not care
what you think about tabs versus spaces.
That’s for a
different
post!  I no longer work for Yelp, anyway — so as compelling as your argument may be, I can no longer undo what I have done.
Prerequisites
First,
be absolutely sure you’re never going to change your mind
.  If you as an organization are ambivalent about your whitespace needs, or if you have influential coworkers who will use this post for evil to switch everything back to tabs as soon as you leave, you may wish to reconsider.
Fix mixed indentation
If you’re using a whitespace-sensitive language, you
must
fix any inconsistent indentation.  (You might want to do this anyway, or your code will look like nonsense.)  By “inconsistent”, I mean any code that will change relative indentation levels if the width of a tab changes. Consider:
1
....if foo:
2
------->print("true")
If a tab is considered to be eight cells wide, as the good Lord intended, this is fine.  But if you’re about to replace all your tabs with four spaces, the extra indentation level vanishes, and suddenly this is invalid Python.
You would not
believe
how many cases of this I found.  I most fondly remember the file that was for some reason indented with
n
tabs
plus
a single space, except where it wasn’t.  I have no idea how that happened.  (Incidentally, the need to micromanage variable-width invisible characters is one of the reasons I wanted to get rid of tabs.)  (Please don’t leave comments about this.)  (Also consider
set shiftround
if you use vim, which pretty well eliminates this problem but is tragically under-used.)
On the other hand, if you are some kind of monster and want to replace every tab with
eight
spaces, then you don’t need to worry about this.
You could just scan your codebase for leading spaces, but if you have a mix of tabbed files and spaced files, you’ll get a ton of false positives and it’ll be a huge pain in the ass.  A somewhat more robust approach for Python specifically is:
1
python
-tt
-m
compileall
.
|
grep
Sorry
-tt
tells the interpreter to treat inconsistent indentation as a
SyntaxError
.  The
compileall
module searches recursively for
.py
files and produces
.pyc
bytecode, which requires parsing each file, which will trigger the
SyntaxError
.  And any errors encountered while compiling modules produce a line starting with
Sorry
, along with the filename, line number, and column number.
Now you can spend an afternoon fixing those all by hand and trying to figure out why this one file seems to have been written with a tabstop of 3.
Distribute a Git filter definition
The actual process uses a
Git filter
to enforce that no new tabs find their way into the repository and fix any tabs on in-flight branches.  The configuration for which filters to run on which files is stored as part of the repository, but unfortunately, the configuration for what each filter
does
is not.
One way or another, you
must
get this block in your devs’ Git configuration — anyone doing regular development who doesn’t have the filter definition will be
utterly
confused.  This is probably the hardest part of the process.  Thankfully, Yelp mostly does work on beefy shared dev machines, so I only had to bug an ops person to stick this incantation in
/etc/gitconfig
and wait for Puppet.
YMMV
.
1
[filter "spabs"]
2
clean = expand --initial -t 4
3
smudge = expand --initial -t 4
4
required
5
[merge]
6
renormalize = true
I’ll explain what this all actually does later.  Oh, and it might help to actually have
expand
installed.  Most Unix-likes should have it already; if you have developers using Windows,
expand
is one of the utilities in the
unixutils
project.  Also,
BSD
(i.e.
OS
X)
expand
apparently doesn’t have the
--initial
argument, but unless you’re in the habit of sprinkling tab characters inside string literals, you can safely leave it off.
Doing it
Here’s the good part.
If at all possible, get all your collaborators to stop doing work for a day while you get this sorted.  Christmas works pretty well!  I did this on December 26, when we were so short-staffed that there weren’t even any deploys scheduled.

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应允许机械性变更提交影响 `git blame`，部分人（如 mmastrac、joshstrange）认为应有机制避免这种影响，而 rurban 则认为无需复杂解决方案。
• 制表符与空格的优劣和使用场景也是一个讨论点，部分人（如 Alifatisk、zzo38computer）质疑或指出某些情况下制表符不应被转换为空格。
• 工具和自动化的使用，如 `.editorconfig` 和 CI 规则，被建议作为确保代码格式一致性的有效手段（gwbas1c）。
• 关于代码风格的个人偏好，如固定宽度字体和不同字符的使用，引发了对程序员习惯的讨论（kgwxd、user9999999999）。

data.title: GitDroid: A third party Android app manager for apps uploaded to GitHub releases
data.author: amadeuspagel
data.article_summary: GitDroid 是一个第三方 Android 应用管理器，用于管理上传到 GitHub 发布的应用。该项目包含一个应用商店，专门用于获取和处理 GitHub 上的应用发布。GitDroid 主要使用 Dart 语言编写，少量使用 Java。目前有 14 个星标，但没有发布正式版本。项目托管在 GitHub 上，并接受赞助支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于不同应用管理工具的比较与使用体验，以及对移动设备生态系统的批评

不同观点：
• Cyphase认为Unobtanium比Obtainium支持更多的来源和功能，并且正在积极开发中，暗示Unobtanium更具优势。
• 0xbadcafebee强烈批评移动设备的应用商店和锁定机制，主张像传统计算机一样自由运行和安装应用程序，强调开放性和持续支持的重要性。
• Sigmonsays表达了对Obtainium的喜爱，但对Unobtanium不了解。
• TechnicJelle作为某应用的开发者，坦承该应用不如Obtainium，并说明因学习目的开发且暂无进一步开发计划。
• 0x073批评某应用的名称与其实际功能不符。
• Rocketvole询问Android平台上Unobtanium和Obtainium的区别，表现出对两者功能差异的困惑。
• Gitroom附和0xbadcafebee的观点，对移动设备锁定机制表示不满，并质疑这种做法背后的真正目的。
• Noname120指出某应用已有两年未更新，质疑其是否功能完备。
• FloatArtifact询问Windows平台上的类似工具，表现出对跨平台解决方案的兴趣。
• Interior推荐Unobtanium，认为Obtainium看起来并不在积极维护中。
• Dengolius提出F-Droid作为一个具有良好图形界面的替代方案，暗示其可能更适合用户需求。
• Yesbut简单支持F-Droid，未做详细说明。
• Sneak提到对微软远程代码执行（RCE）的担忧，暗示对依赖GitHub等平台的安全性问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是移动设备应用管理工具的必要性和现有工具的优劣，比如Unobtanium与Obtainium的功能对比。
• 另一个焦点是移动设备生态系统的封闭性和锁定机制，用户对此表达了不满，并讨论了这种机制对用户自由和设备寿命的影响。
• 安全性问题也被提及，特别是对依赖于某些平台的工具和应用的潜在安全风险的担忧。

总结：讨论围绕应用管理工具的功能、开发状态及其在不同平台上的替代方案展开，同时对移动设备生态系统的开放性和安全性提出了质疑。

data.title: Connomore64: Cycle exact emulation of the C64 using parallel microcontrollers
data.author: codewiz
data.article_summary: Connomore64 是一个使用多个微控制器并行运行的Commodore 64（C64）计算机的实时循环精确仿真项目。该项目旨在通过廉价的RP2040/RP2350微控制器（每芯片不到1欧元）重建C64，通过8位多路复用总线以约8 MHz的有效速度互连，使用DVI/HDMI输出视频和音频，并精确模拟原始硬件信号时序。它可以与C1541软驱和一些扩展硬件接口，支持快速加载器。此外，它也是一个示例，展示了如何在廉价低功耗的互连微控制器上运行计算密集型软件，并作为调试和测试多个RP2040/RP2350并行项目的仿真框架。该项目起源于2022年圣诞节的业余项目，目标是探索RP2040微控制器的潜力，特别是其PIO（GPIO处理协处理器）。与现有简化版的C64仿真器不同，Connomore64追求精确的循环和时序仿真，同时兼容物理 retro 硬件。硬件方面，使用了自定义PCB（Breadbox v0原型），支持C64的常用端口和HDMI、音频输出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕C64 SID芯片及相关硬件、仿真器项目的讨论，包括技术细节、实际应用以及怀旧情感。

不同观点：
• rollcat：对SID芯片声音的热爱，分享了与SID芯片相关的项目和艺术家链接。对实际项目和艺术创作的积极评价。
• bitwize：讨论了通过多个CPU分别仿真不同组件以实现精确时序仿真的技术想法，并对该想法的实现表示赞赏，但指出细节处理的复杂性。
• sandos：最初误以为该项目可以用来替换C64的损坏部件，但发现并非如此。表达了理解和接受。
• wiz21c：对图形渲染代码重写后速度提升但兼容性下降表示遗憾，质疑选择这种做法的原因。
• abhisek：虽然不热衷于硬件，但因为怀旧而尝试构建仿真器，分享了学习经历。
• sunpazed：表达了对C64的怀旧情感，拥有近40年历史的C64，担心其损坏。对该项目的实用性表示赞赏。
• gitroom：赞赏人们为保持C64运行所做的努力，激发了自己修复旧设备的兴趣。
• eabeezxjc：支持该解决方案，并建议在其上运行fuzix.org，提出开放性的建议。
• chillingeffect：热爱修复C64，分享了自己的修复经验和成本，对使用Rpi pico替代CIA芯片的可能性表示好奇，并提出了技术细节问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：wiz21c对仿真器项目在追求速度的同时牺牲兼容性表示不满，质疑其技术选择。
• 技术细节：bitwize和chillingeffect对仿真技术细节和硬件替代方案进行了深入讨论，包括多CPU仿真和使用现代硬件替代旧部件的可能性。
• 怀旧和情感：多个评论者（sunpazed、abhisek、gitroom）表达了对C64的怀旧情感和对旧设备修复的热情。

Connomore64
https://github.com/c1570/Connomore64
Realtime cycle exact emulation of the
Commodore 64
using multiple microcontrollers in parallel.
This is a proof of concept and not end user ready.
July 2024 poster
(old prototype)
In a nutshell, this is (or aims to be)…
…a
cycle exact Commodore 64 homecomputer emulator
…
…an (almost) chip-by-chip rebuild using multiple
RP2040
/
RP2350
microcontrollers (<1€ per chip!)…
…interconnected using a multiplexed
8 bit bus
running at about 8 MHz effectively…
…using
DVI/HDMI
as video and audio output…
…with microsecond exact true to original real world signal timing…
…able to
interface with original hardware
…
…such as the C1541 floppy drive, including fastloaders…
…as well as userport and (some) expansion port based hardware.
Additionally, this is…
…an example of running
compute intensive software on cheap low powered interconnected microcontrollers
…
…an
emulation framework
to test and debug projects using several RP2040/RP2350s in parallel on a PC.
But why?
First and foremost, this was started as a holiday project (“porting an existing C64 emulator to a 400MHz ARM platform cannot take that long, can it?”) with a focus on playing a bit with the RP2040 microcontroller and getting an idea of what its PIOs (i.e., its GPIO handling coprocessors) are capable of.
The holiday of this “holiday project” was christmas 2022, and it turns out a single 400MHz M0+ core is definitely not enough to emulate a C64, if accuracy is some priority…
While a C64 emulator on the RP2040 already
exists
, it is using an extremely simplified model of the C64, e.g., not emulating the exact steps and timing of MOS 6510 CPU opcodes, and not emulating the VIC-II video chip exactly but doing video line based emulation instead which limits compatibility.
PC based emulators (VICE, BMC etc.) reach high emulation quality but do not feature perfect realtime timing. That means you cannot use physical retro hardware (floppy drives, etc.) with those emulators in general.
FPGA based emulators of the C64 reach high emulation quality and realtime accuracy, but those platforms strike yours truly as quite overpowered and expensive, not as hackable as would be nice, and typically come with a rather unwieldy (and typically closed source) toolchain.
Building Blocks
RP2040/RP2350 Emulator
For developing this project, the
rp2040js
emulator project by Uri Shaked of
Wokwi.com
fame has been extended. Very little debugging on real hardware happened. No logic analyzers were necessary at all!
You can find my fork of rp2040js
here
. It features:
RP2350 support (RISC-V/Hazard3 only)
cycle exact timing of PIOs
VCD
trace files can get generated for the GPIO signals
a simple framework for running multiple chip emulation instances interfacing to each other (
WIP code
)
simulation of input/output latency of GPIOs
functionality to output statistics and monitor any PIO stalls is present in the emulation runner that has been customized for this project
C64 Emulator Code
The C64 emulation code is based on the “
chips
” emulation library by Andre Weissflog. A lot of optimizations have been done:
speed optimized VIC-II code
rewritten graphics rendering code (running 5-10 times as fast as the previous code while sacrificing some compatibility)
rendering bitmap/text mode is done using PIO/DMA
rewritten Sprite rendering (in contrast to the original VIC-II, sprites are rendered into a buffer in the offscreen time)
fixed a few
VIC-II emulation bugs
(VSP/AGSP works now)
faster CIA emulation using look up tables
replaced
uint64_t pins
interface with 32 bits pins/direct variables
Video Output
HDMI/DVI output is based on the
PicoDVI
library by Luke Wren.
Audio Output
Provided by a port of the
SIDKick pico
firmware (by Carsten Dachsbacher, using reSID by Dag Lem) to the Connomore64 bus system.
Hardware
Breadbox v0 prototype (latest)
This is a custom PCB that fits into the C64 case (shown on top of the page).
It comes with the usual C64 ports (userport, IEC, expansion port, joystick ports) plus HDMI and audio jack.
Currently, the userport, IEC, and joystick ports are functional.
Support for select expansion port cartridges (e.g., Magic Desk) is upcoming.
Goals of this prototype:
All original C64 connectors available
Simple to build
Easy migration to RP2350 in development
Testbed for SWD-based firmware handling
Stacked Pico boards (early prototype)
The first pro

data.title: Creating Bluey: Tales from the Art Director
data.author: cfcfcf
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕创意产业的价值分配、地域性对职业发展的影响以及创意工作中的工作条件等问题展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **创意工作的价值分配不公**：[polotics] 指出，创意工作者如《Bluey》艺术总监的工资与其创造的价值严重不匹配，仅有极小部分的价值返回到工作者手中。这种不公平的分配使得创意工作难以维持，并认为创意工作在本社会中注定会失败。
  
• **地域对职业发展的影响**：[JohnScolaro] 表达了作为布里斯班软件开发者的挣扎，认为布里斯班相对于墨尔本、悉尼以及美国的科技中心来说是“落后”的。尽管如此，他依然热爱布里斯班，并希望在这里取得成功，但也意识到去像西雅图这样的城市工作可能会带来更多行业经验。

• **创意工作与工作条件的平衡**：[aaronbrethorst] 强调不应为了创造一个好的作品而牺牲员工的健康和福祉。他提到自己会避免那些以“创作伟大作品”为借口压榨员工的工作，并认为可以创造伟大的作品而不必“杀死你的团队”。

• **对创意过程的欣赏**：[meander_water] 表达了对设计师能力的欣赏，认为设计师能够根据需求通过自己的艺术表达来赋予作品生命。此外，[fuzzfactor] 提到通过创造自己真正想创造的东西，能够吸引到让自己满意的机会和工作，这适用于艺术和科学领域。

补充讨论：

data.title: ePub-utils: A Python library and CLI tool for inspecting ePub from the terminal
data.author: ernstgnzlz
data.article_summary: **epub-utils** 是一个用于处理 EPUB 文件的 Python 命令行工具和实用库。它可以解析和验证 EPUB 文件的容器及包文件，提取标题、作者、标识符等元数据。该工具提供命令行接口，用于快速检查文件内容，如显示 `container.xml`、`package OPF` 及目录等。同时，它也可以作为 Python 库使用，通过 `Document` 类加载 EPUB 文件并访问其元数据。安装方法为通过 `pip install epub-utils` 进行安装。该项目遵循 Apache-2.0 开源许可证。

不同观点：
• Flex247A 分享了自己开发的EPUB阅读器项目，该项目使用系统Webview渲染EPUB文档。

A Python CLI and utility library for manipulating EPUB files.
Features

epub-utils your-book.epub container

data.title: Open-source AI platform for ear-based sensing applications
data.author: vyrotek
data.article_summary: OpenEarable是全球首个开源的耳戴式传感AI平台，集成了高精度传感器和真无线音频技术。该平台专为开发和研究设计，具备模块化、可重构和面向未来的特点。其硬件包括USB-C接口、纽扣电池、9轴IMU、气导麦克风、压力传感器、骨传导麦克风、动态驱动扬声器、PPG光学温度传感器等。OpenEarable支持多种传感功能，如耳道认证、心脏监测、声学追踪、皮肤温度检测等，适用于睡眠呼吸暂停检测、压力监测、运动追踪等多种应用。平台采用Nordic nRF5340双核处理器和ADAU1860音频处理DSP，兼具高性能和低功耗，支持蓝牙传输和内部SD卡记录，提供广泛的应用潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放源代码硬件耳机的项目及其可行性、价格、技术细节和潜在应用

不同观点：
• [shae]：认为2500欧元的价格对于个人娱乐项目过高，虽然对项目本身感兴趣，但因为预算限制无法购买。之前购买过价格较为合理的Tympan开源助听器（约300美元）。期望该产品价格下降后能用于一些有趣的项目。
• [eloycoto]：对项目表示赞赏，特别提到BMA550加速度计用于检测语音和静音功能非常酷。同时质疑IMU（惯性测量单元）代码中未使用MM-FIT的部分，整体对产品持积极态度。
• [Etheryte]：对苹果公司在未来可能采纳此类技术表示期待，认为尽管苹果在AI方面最近表现不佳，但其在缩小产品尺寸和利用iPhone芯片进行计算方面的能力很强。不过，苹果需要先解决当前的问题。
• [djtango]：对项目的实际用途感到困惑，请求简单解释（ELI5：像我五岁一样解释）。
• [Swain123]：表示对开放源代码耳机的需求，之前关注过Pine Buds Pro，但因关税或价格问题未能购买。强调工程和黑客社区对开源耳机有很大需求。
• [victorbjorklund]：认为价格过高，可能更像是一个开发套件，希望像苹果这样的公司能采纳并推广这项技术。
• [MeteorMarc]：关心耳机的重量，担心过重会导致头痛，同时认为从图片看还有进一步微型化的可能。

补充讨论：
• 价格是讨论中的一个主要争议点，尤其是对于个人用户和开发者而言，2500欧元的价格被普遍认为过高。
• 技术细节如BMA550加速度计和IMU的功能及其实现也是讨论的重点，体现出技术社区对项目细节的关注。
• 潜在应用和市场前景，尤其是苹果等大公司可能采纳和推广这项技术的可能性，引发了对未来发展的期待。
• 产品的重量和微型化潜力也被提及，反映出用户对佩戴舒适度和设计优化的关注。

争议焦点：
• 价格过高与潜在用户需求之间的矛盾是主要争议点，用户普遍希望价格下降以增加可获得性和实用性。

• [victorbjorklund]：认为价格过高，可能更像是一个开发套件，希望像苹果这样的公司能采纳并推广这项技术。
• [MeteorMarc]：关心耳机的重量，担心过重会导致头痛，同时认为从图片看还有进一步微型化的可能。

补充讨论：
• 价格是讨论中的一个主要争议点，尤其是对于个人用户和开发者而言，2500欧元的价格被普遍认为过高。
• 技术细节如BMA550加速度计和IMU的功能及其实现也是讨论的重点，体现出技术社区对项目细节的关注。
• 潜在应用和市场前景，尤其是苹果等大公司可能采纳和推广这项技术的可能性，引发了对未来发展的期待。
• 产品的重量和微型化潜力也被提及，反映出用户对佩戴舒适度和设计优化的关注。

争议焦点：
• 价格过高与潜在用户需求之间的矛盾是主要争议点，用户普遍希望价格下降以增加可获得性和实用性。

data.title: The future of solar doesn't track the sun
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了东西固定太阳能阵列是否比单轴跟踪阵列更经济。尽管单轴跟踪阵列在每块面板的能量产出上仍占优势，且在严重冰雹等恶劣天气下更具抵御能力，但东西固定阵列具有安装速度更快、材料和劳动力成本更低的优势，且占地更少。随着光伏组件价格的下降，东西阵列的经济优势愈发明显。如果仅考虑每瓦交付价格，东西阵列显然是更优选择，但在一些地区，由于技术 resilience 不足，单轴阵列仍有其必要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳能系统的不同设计和优化方案，包括固定阵列、东西方向阵列、追踪系统和垂直安装等，以及各自的优缺点和实际应用。

不同观点：
• adamcharnock认为固定阵列在离网环境下已经足够，但在日出和日落时需要额外电力，考虑过增加东西方向的阵列，但因复杂性而放弃。
• mchannon拥有丰富的太阳能行业经验，指出东西方向阵列是一种新颖的设计，不同于传统的固定倾斜或追踪系统，呼吁人们更深入地理解这种新设计。
• weinzierl通过早期的研究和实验，发现追踪系统的机械可靠性是一个主要问题，并提出使用简单机械齿轮来提高可靠性，但最终认为移动方案的利润不理想。
• edent实际安装了东西方向的屋顶太阳能，发现效率低于纯南向，但能更平稳地发电，并在晚上提供更多电力。
• tgsovlerkhgsel指出追踪阵列在早晚发电的优势，并讨论了安装双倍固定面板与追踪系统的经济性对比。
• tzs提出使用DMD设备实现部分追踪，通过机械可靠性更高的微镜设备来提高发电效率。
• rini17建议垂直安装面板以减少冰雹和雪的影响，并通过南北方向排列来最大化早晚发电。
• mr_world对利用太阳能板发电产生天然气持怀疑态度，认为这可能不利于气候变化。
• xphos认为单轴追踪系统能使每块板的发电曲线更一致，并好奇更多固定板是否能在规模上标准化生产。
• nbadg关注冰雹损害问题，提出自动展开防冰雹网的中庸方案，以降低机械负荷。
• tmjdev质疑太阳能成本数据的来源，尤其是消费者层面的成本。
• wyldfire关注住宅太阳能安装成本，认为人工成本可能成为主要部分。
• Simulacra误以为文章是关于不追踪太阳的太阳能烟囱。

补充讨论：
• 各种方案的机械复杂性和可靠性是讨论的重点，尤其是追踪系统的可靠性和维护成本。
• 经济性是另一个重要讨论点，包括追踪系统与固定阵列的成本效益对比。
• 实际应用中的特殊情况，如冰雹防护和早晚电力需求，也被多次提及。
• 不同设计方案的发电效率和平稳性在多个评论中被比较和讨论。

43861253.article_content:
PV modules are cheap enough today that the simple fixed East-West arrays are cheaper and faster to install than the industry’s darling, the single-axis tracked array.
Xavier Dedenbach, Terraform Power Electronics Engineer
Originally posted
on April 20, 2025.
Summary
This article takes you on a journey to explore whether East-West fixed solar arrays are now more economical than the dominant variant, single-axis tracked arrays. If you just want the answer, feel free to jump to the end or read this summary. But if you have 15 minutes to follow along, the juice is worth the squeeze.
We’re
hiring at Terraform
!
💡
Today’s Claim
PV modules are cheap enough today that the simple fixed East-West arrays are cheaper and faster to install than the industry’s darling, the single-axis tracked array.
Arguments Against
Single-axis tracked arrays still significantly outperform East-West fixed arrays in energy production on a per-panel basis.
There is one weather pattern (severe hail) so destructive that I would choose the more expensive single-axis tracked array if I experienced it regularly.
Arguments For
East-West arrays require less material and labor to install.
East-West arrays use substantially less land for the same power output.
As PV modules become cheaper, the economic benefits of East-West arrays get even better.
Conclusion
If price per watt delivered were the only important factor, East-West arrays would be the clear choice everywhere.
However, nature is metal, and in some regions, we currently lack sufficiently resilient panel technology to support East-West arrays.
Introduction
Like many technologies, photovoltaic (PV) cells, which convert sunlight into usable energy, started out expensive and uncompetitive. They had to compete in one of the most competitive industrial sectors: the energy sector, which is filled with behemoths like coal, natural gas, and hydropower. On top of that, photovoltaic technology was handicapped by limited daylight hours and an above-average vulnerability to weather conditions.
PV systems did not have it easy, but a collective push from green energy companies, governments, and their citizens willed them into existence. They shared in the renewable energy promise to build an economy powered by sunlight, wind, water, and atoms.
So began the decades-long push to improve module efficiency in every way imaginable: new materials, new
PV cell architectures that convert more photons to electrons
, and tracking systems that keep modules aligned with the Sun’s position. These trackers gained industry dominance by offsetting their costs through improved efficiency of the PV modules.
Today’s story examines what happens when the very components being optimized, the PV modules themselves, become cheaper than the technologies designed to improve their efficiency.
Figure 1:
Choose your characters. The incumbent tracking solution vs the simple East-West solution.
Tracking technologies are moderately complex, requiring actuators, sensors, stronger structures, and additional energy storage. These technologies fall into two camps: single-axis and dual-axis systems. Single-axis trackers handle intra-day solar movements, following the Sun as it rises in the East and sets in the West. Dual-axis trackers adjust for the array’s latitude, the Sun’s intra-day movement, and inter-day movement, due to Earth’s orbit
1
. Unlike single-axis trackers, dual-axis solutions haven’t seen mass adoption due to more complicated mechanisms and increased spacing requirements between rows to prevent shading. For this reason, we’ll focus solely on the costs and benefits of the single-axis tracker, the current king, if you will, and its relation to its much simpler cousin, Earl. Ugh… I mean the East-West array.
The Rapid Decline in PV Module Prices
Why ask this question? When I took over the solar and power systems at Terraform Industries, I was asked to architect a photovoltaic system that capitalized on one of the most remarkable learning curves in modern history: a 44% cost reduction for every doubling of cumulative PV module production. The East-West array was a clear winner, despite not being highly adopted in the United States. I began to investigate why, and this article is a byproduct of this effort.
Starting with PV module costs, PV benefited from the trifecta of expanding economies of scale, increased competition as more suppliers rushed into the market, and increased supply as high-grade silicon became abundant due to the demand for PV modules and integrated circuits, aka chips. That level of cost reduction is hard to compete with. In the 2010s, the cost of PV modules fell by 85%, and so far this decade, they have fallen an additional 58%. All this in the face of the worldwide epidemic of increased inflation in recent years.
Table 1:
Module Price Reduction 2010-2025
Over the last decade, trackers rose to dominance, and by 2015, they accounted for more than 50% of the cumulative installed capacity for photovoltaic syst

data.title: Game preservationists say Switch2 GameKey Cards are disheartening but inevitable
data.author: haunter
data.article_summary: Nintendo Switch 2引入了Game-Key Cards，这些卡片并不包含完整游戏数据，仅作为下载游戏的“钥匙”。玩家需要通过互联网从Switch 2在线商店下载游戏。尽管插入卡片后可以像普通实体卡一样启动游戏，但若未来服务器关闭，这些卡片可能无法使用。游戏保护人士对此表示担忧，认为这不利于游戏保存，而也有观点认为卡带上的游戏常通过补丁更新，实体卡本身更多是数字版权保护工具。业内人士指出，游戏全面数字化是不可避免的趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏 preservation（保存）、数字版权管理、以及游戏分发模式的变化对玩家体验的影响。

不同观点：
• [xg15] 认为任天堂不重视游戏 preservation，公司更关注品牌和旧游戏的记忆，而不是游戏本身的保存，因为这样可以通过重制版和复刻版进行再 monetization（货币化）。
• [proc0] 认为保存游戏不应围绕硬件，而是应关注玩家是否有权为个人使用创建数字备份。现代问题已不再是盗版，而是将游戏作为服务提供，以便进行更多 monetization。
• [jsheard] 建议任天堂可以采用类似于 Xbox/PlayStation 的模式，通过光盘分发并安装到 SSD，而不是完全依赖在线服务来玩实体游戏。
• [j1elo] 反对游戏机对互联网的依赖，认为这对没有稳定互联网连接的玩家不友好，并提到通过破解设备使用盗版内容是一种无奈但有效的解决方案。
• [mysteria] 指出游戏行业逐渐转向下载模式，而云游戏的趋势可能会完全防止盗版，但这也意味着玩家无法真正“拥有”游戏，而是按月付费。
• [qbane] 强调即使是发布当天的游戏版本也值得保存，因为有些社区（如 speedrun 社区）需要精确的游戏版本进行比赛，而频繁的更新和补丁使得物理拷贝变得不稳定。
• [dmwilcox] 表示自己从不需要在线功能，并希望游戏机能像90年代的GameBoy一样简单，没有多余的网络、社交功能。
• [kmeisthax] 讨论了日本市场的特殊性，指出日本版Switch 2有显著不同的销售策略，包括区域和语言锁定，这影响了国际玩家的体验。
• [hombre_fatal] 认为无论是实体还是数字游戏，玩家最终都会受到硬件寿命或在线商店关闭的影响，数字游戏的购买无法像实体游戏一样持久。
• [mcphage] 认为任天堂使用卡带而非光盘有其合理和不合理的理由，卡带的高成本是现代游戏的一个问题，但卡带也可以看作是数字游戏的可转移许可。
• [QuadmasterXLII] 指出实体光盘游戏即使能玩，也往往需要零日补丁，而下载版游戏则容易随服务器关闭而消失。
• [ferguess_k] 认为Switch只是在跟随其他主机的发展趋势，并提出是否存在不需要依赖模拟器的8-bit/16-bit/32-bit原生掌机市场，可能只是小众爱好者的市场。
• [addoo] 认为现代实体媒介游戏几乎都需要零日补丁，而公司很少提供旧版本的游戏，导致许多有趣的旧版本游戏已经“丢失”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是游戏 preservation 是否应由公司负责，以及如何在现代数字分发模式下有效保存游戏，特别是当公司频繁更新和下架游戏时。
• 另一个焦点是游戏机对互联网依赖的增加，特别是对没有互联网连接的玩家造成的不便。
• 数字版权管理和物理媒介的对比，以及如何在数字时代保护玩家的长期权益也是讨论的重要内容。
• 日本市场的特殊情况及其对国际玩家的影响也被详细讨论，包括区域锁定和语言锁定等问题。

GO AD-FREE! Support VGC on Patreon for exclusive content & features
Support VGC
Game preservationists have been giving their opinions on Nintendo Switch 2’s new Game-Key Cards.
Game-Key Cards are
Nintendo
âs new branding for cartridges that still require the game to be downloaded from the
Switch 2
online store before the game can be played. The cartridge doesnât contain the game data, rather itâs simply a âkeyâ that enables a download.
âGame-key cards are different from regular game cards, because they donât contain the full game data,â Nintendo’s own description says. âInstead, the game-key card is your âkeyâ to downloading the full game to your system via the internet. After itâs downloaded, you can play the game by inserting the game-key card into your system and starting it up like a standard physical game card.â
So far the vast majority of third-party Switch 2 games are Game-Key Cards, with only a few exceptions such as
Cyberpunk 2077
and the Western version of
Daemon X Machina
: Titanic Scion.
When Japanese store Yodobashi started listing Switch 2 games, of the 11 new third-party Switch 2 games initially listed on the site with box art,
all 11 had a logo on the front of the box designating them as Game-Key Cards
.
The issue some players have with Game-Key Cards is that because they don’t contain the full game content on the cartridge, should the Switch 2 shop servers ever close down in the distant future â and therefore no longer provide the downloads necessary â those cartridges may become unplayable.
Most third-party Switch 2 games on the Yodobashi site are Game-Key Cards (as noted by the white bar on the bottom of the box).
In a new report by
GamesIndustry.biz
, several people involved in game preservation and re-releases have given their views on the situation.
Stephen Kick, CEO of
Nightdive Studios
(which specialises in modern remasters of older, often out-of-print games) said that “seeing Nintendo do this is a little disheartening”, adding: “You would hope that a company that big, that has such a storied history, would take preservation a little more seriously.”
Videogame Heritage Society co-founder Professor James Newman is somewhat less convinced that Game-Key Cards will be a major issue, noting that it’s rare for a game on a cartridge to still be the same game years after release.
“Even when a cartridge does contain data on day one of release, games are so often patched, updated and expanded through downloads that the cart very often loses its connection to the game, and functions more like a physical copy protection dongle for a digital object,” he explained.
Meanwhile, Paul Dyson, director of the International Center for the History of Electronic Games at The Strong Museum in New York said the move to a future where all games are digital is “inevitable”, and that Nintendo has in fact been “in some ways, the slowest of the major console producers to be going there”.

• [mysteria] 指出游戏行业逐渐转向下载模式，而云游戏的趋势可能会完全防止盗版，但这也意味着玩家无法真正“拥有”游戏，而是按月付费。
• [qbane] 强调即使是发布当天的游戏版本也值得保存，因为有些社区（如 speedrun 社区）需要精确的游戏版本进行比赛，而频繁的更新和补丁使得物理拷贝变得不稳定。
• [dmwilcox] 表示自己从不需要在线功能，并希望游戏机能像90年代的GameBoy一样简单，没有多余的网络、社交功能。
• [kmeisthax] 讨论了日本市场的特殊性，指出日本版Switch 2有显著不同的销售策略，包括区域和语言锁定，这影响了国际玩家的体验。
• [hombre_fatal] 认为无论是实体还是数字游戏，玩家最终都会受到硬件寿命或在线商店关闭的影响，数字游戏的购买无法像实体游戏一样持久。
• [mcphage] 认为任天堂使用卡带而非光盘有其合理和不合理的理由，卡带的高成本是现代游戏的一个问题，但卡带也可以看作是数字游戏的可转移许可。
• [QuadmasterXLII] 指出实体光盘游戏即使能玩，也往往需要零日补丁，而下载版游戏则容易随服务器关闭而消失。
• [ferguess_k] 认为Switch只是在跟随其他主机的发展趋势，并提出是否存在不需要依赖模拟器的8-bit/16-bit/32-bit原生掌机市场，可能只是小众爱好者的市场。
• [addoo] 认为现代实体媒介游戏几乎都需要零日补丁，而公司很少提供旧版本的游戏，导致许多有趣的旧版本游戏已经“丢失”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是游戏 preservation 是否应由公司负责，以及如何在现代数字分发模式下有效保存游戏，特别是当公司频繁更新和下架游戏时。
• 另一个焦点是游戏机对互联网依赖的增加，特别是对没有互联网连接的玩家造成的不便。
• 数字版权管理和物理媒介的对比，以及如何在数字时代保护玩家的长期权益也是讨论的重要内容。
• 日本市场的特殊情况及其对国际玩家的影响也被详细讨论，包括区域锁定和语言锁定等问题。

data.title: PScientists reveal how bats learn to identify which prey is safe to eat
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 科学家在史密森热带研究所（STRI）发现，边缘唇蝠（fringe-lipped bat）通过经验学习区分可食和有毒的青蛙与蟾蜍。这种蝙蝠通过窃听蛙类求偶叫声来捕猎，但幼年蝙蝠不像成年蝙蝠那样能准确辨别叫声中的危险信号。研究显示，幼蝠最初只能通过叫声判断猎物的大小，而对毒性的辨别能力则需随着时间发展。成年蝙蝠能有效避免追逐有毒或过大猎物，而幼年蝙蝠则需通过学习逐步提高这种辨别能力。该研究首次证明了这种窃听捕食者在成长过程中会调整其对猎物声音线索的反应。

• 该评论没有直接回应grues-dinner的观点，而是通过提供一篇关于动物行为研究的学术文章链接（wglb）来引导讨论。这篇文章可能涉及动物是否具有类似人类的意识或行为模式，从而间接回应PScientist是否类似于哲学僵尸的问题。

补充讨论：
• petemir的评论带有一些哲思和感慨，似乎是在感叹人类若能像PScientist或哲学僵尸那样单纯依赖行为模式而无需内在意识，可能会带来某些好处或简化。这暗示了对人类意识复杂性及其潜在负担的反思。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于PScientist是否真的类似于哲学僵尸，即它们是否只是行为上像科学家，而缺乏真正的理解和意识。这一问题触及了人工智能和人类意识之间界限的哲学讨论。

总结：
该评论串涉及对PScientist本质属性的哲学类比，探讨其是否类似于哲学僵尸。同时，通过引入相关学术文章，讨论扩展到动物行为和人类意识的复杂性，并引发对意识存在意义的进一步思考。

Palatable versus poisonous: Scientists reveal how bats learn to identify which prey is safe to eat
by
Smithsonian
A fringe-lipped bat, Trachops cirrhosus, approaches a Fitzinger's robber frog, Craugastor fitzingeri, in Panama. This species of bat eavesdrops on the mating calls that male frogs produce to attract females, and uses these frog calls to detect, assess and localize its prey. Young bats do not share the same responses to frog mating calls that adults do; juveniles must acquire the ability to discriminate which frog calls signify palatable and poisonous prey. Credit: Merlin Tuttle
Scientists at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI) found that the fringe-lipped bat, known to eavesdrop on frog and toad mating calls to find its prey, learns to distinguish between palatable and unpalatable frogs and toads through experience.
The findings, published in the
Proceedings of the Royal Society B
, provide the first evidence that eavesdropping predators fine-tune their hunting cues over the course of their development.
To source their food, some predators eavesdrop on calls emitted by prey. Fringe-lipped bats, which range from Panama to Brazil, are some of the most skilled eavesdroppers in the world. They are attuned to the sexual advertisement calls of over a dozen frog and toad species that live in their habitat. If a fringe-lipped bat hears a call, it will fly toward the sound within seconds.
However, just like some incoming calls on people's cell phones originate from scammers, not every frog or toad call guarantees a safe and healthy meal—if a frog is too large or emits a toxin, the prey can pose a danger to the bat.
A fringe-lipped bat, Trachops cirrhosus, responds to the calls of the túngara frog, Engystomops pustulosus, one of its preferred prey species. First, the bat hears the call of a single male túngara frog, producing a complex call (a 'whine' plus multiple 'chucks'.) Then, the bat hears the cacophony of a large túngara frog chorus, with many male túngara frogs acoustically competing for females at once. Credit: Joseph See
Fringe-lipped bats have adapted to this risk by developing their own caller ID; if they hear a call from an unpalatable frog or toad, they save their time and energy by not responding. But frog and toad calls do not come with automatic "spam" warnings like
phone calls
do, and until now, scientists did not know where the fringe-lipped bat's ability to distinguish between palatable and unpalatable frogs came from.
"It's truly remarkable that these bats hunt using the calls of an entirely different group of animals in the first place, and we have wondered for a long time how these bats acquire this unusual skill," said Logan James, STRI postdoctoral researcher and lead author of the study.
"We knew from previous research that these bats are very clever and can learn during experiments, but we had not tested whether their aptitude for learning had a role in fine-tuning their responses to sound cues from their natural prey."
A fringe-lipped bat, Trachops cirrhosus, hears a male túngara frog, Engystomops pustulosus, producing an advertisement call to attract a mate. The bat approaches the calling frog, but the frog detects it in time, stops calling and ducks, successfully avoiding the eavesdropping predator. Credit: Joseph See
The research team tested how individual, wild-caught adult and juvenile fringe-lipped bats responded to mating call recordings of 15 local
frog
and toad species. These species included frogs known to be palatable, toxic or too large to handle.
First, the team confirmed previous studies showing that adult bats responded more strongly to palatable versus unpalatable frogs and toads. Yet, as the team discovered, juvenile bats did not make the same distinctions. On average, juvenile bats did not respond differently to frogs and toads based on their palatability.
Looking more closely, the team found that juveniles could identify larger prey by their calls, just like adults can, but they could not distinguish the toxic species. This indicates that juveniles tend to respond to body size early on, but they learn to identify toxic species over time.
A fringe-lipped bat, Trachops cirrhosus, returns to its perch after a successful hunt, and consumes its prey, a túngara frog, Engystomops pustulosus.. Credit: Joseph See
"We have studied this fascinating species for years, and in many aspects, we understand its behavior very well," said Rachel Page, staff scientist at STRI, and one of the study's senior authors.

data.title: N8n – Flexible AI workflow automation for technical teams
data.author: XCSme
data.article_summary: n8n是一个灵活的工作流自动化平台，专为技术团队设计，结合了代码的精确性和拖放界面的便捷性。用户可以选择自建主机或云端托管，实现多步骤AI代理和应用集成。平台支持自然语言命令转换、客户洞察生成等多种功能，适用于IT运维、安全运维、开发运维和销售等多个领域。n8n提供1700多个模板，支持JavaScript和Python编写，并允许添加npm或Python库。该平台拥有超过20万社区成员，并获得G2上4.9/5的评分。企业版提供全面的安全、性能和协作功能，诸如全权控制、加密存储和Git集成等。众多企业通过n8n大幅提升了工作效率，如Delivery Hero每月节省200小时。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：n8n的功能、使用体验及其与AI的结合

不同观点：
• [jasongill] 认为n8n是一个类似于Zapier的自托管工具，具有许多内置集成，但定制"应用程序"（触发器或工作流目的地）的功能较差，且需要通过JavaScript模块和Docker容器操作，不够专业。虽然n8n在某些方面不如企业级解决方案成熟，但相比Windmill，n8n更受非技术用户的欢迎。总体上，n8n值得一试，但超出基础功能时需要一些调整。
• [photon_garden] 指出n8n在可观察性、非技术人员使用和集成方面表现良好，但在并行执行、版本控制和定价方面存在不足。如果公司有工程能力，直接写后端代码可能更简单快速。
• [ChrisGammell] 分享了一次使用n8n将多个API粘合在一起的经验，认为它非常适合在没有无服务器/Lambda的情况下进行外部计算的原型设计。
• [fzysingularity] 表示n8n在内部自动化（如Reddit/HN抓取、Slack自动化、销售定时任务等）方面表现出色，并开发了自定义节点用于文档/图像/视频的ETL工作。
• [hypefi] 认为在AI可以完成大量编码工作的时代，直接使用代码进行自动化可能比使用n8n更好，但n8n的视觉方面（AI代理节点、链和工作流）值得关注。
• [preya2k] 推荐Windmill作为n8n的开放源代码替代方案。
• [nico] 希望了解n8n的成功使用案例，以更好地理解其实际应用场景。
• [kfogel] 提到n8n曾因使用非开放源代码许可证但自称"开放源代码"而引发争议，强调保持"开放源代码"术语特异性的重要性。
• [Jefro118] 询问如何将网站/网页抓取步骤集成到更大的工作流中，并考虑将浏览器RPA工具集成到n8n中。
• [SKILNER] 质疑n8n的名称是否反映了其产品的用户体验。
• [MattDaEskimo] 认为无代码工作流构建器往往无法达到正确的抽象层次，尤其是引入新范式时。
• [behnamoh] 关注n8n在教育领域的应用，特别是对于没有CS背景的学生，寻找免费开放源代码解决方案以供学生毕业后使用。
• [victorbjorklund] 表示自己多年来自托管n8n，认为它非常出色。
• [Izmaki] 认为n8n是将AI和管道技术结合的产物，虽然不讨厌AI，但对AI被强行塞入每个产品或技术中感到不满。
• [bwfan123] 质疑n8n所谓的AI功能，认为它只是几十年来一直存在的工作流自动化。

补充讨论：
• n8n的AI功能被多位用户质疑其实际用途和必要性，认为更多是市场宣传的噱头。
• 用户对n8n的定制功能、并行执行、版本控制和定价等方面的不足提出了具体批评。
• 有多个用户提到n8n在教育领域和非技术用户中的潜在应用价值，但也指出了其在用户权限管理和SSO方面的不足。
• 对n8n是否真正符合"开放源代码"的定义存在历史争议，反映出对术语使用准确性的关注。

• [MattDaEskimo] 认为无代码工作流构建器往往无法达到正确的抽象层次，尤其是引入新范式时。

• [victorbjorklund] 表示自己多年来自托管n8n，认为它非常出色。
• [Izmaki] 认为n8n是将AI和管道技术结合的产物，虽然不讨厌AI，但对AI被强行塞入每个产品或技术中感到不满。

• n8n的AI功能被多位用户质疑其实际用途和必要性，认为更多是市场宣传的噱头。

• 有多个用户提到n8n在教育领域和非技术用户中的潜在应用价值，但也指出了其在用户权限管理和SSO方面的不足。

data.title: Closures in Tcl
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了Tcl编程语言中闭包的概念及其模拟方法。作者首先提到Tcl/Tk 9.0发布后，社区对缺乏闭包功能的讨论。接着，作者解释了闭包的定义，并通过C++和Python的例子进行比较，指出C++中的闭包是通过值捕获变量，而Python则支持更灵活的闭包机制。在Tcl中，虽然没有原生的闭包支持，但可以通过一些技巧来模拟实现。文章详细介绍了如何在Tcl中实现类似闭包的功能，并探讨了不同编程语言中闭包的实现差异。最后，作者分享了自己对Tcl的喜爱以及其优缺点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程语言中的闭包和变量捕获行为，特别是C++、Rust和Tcl，以及对多范式编程语言的讨论。

不同观点：
• **C++中的闭包与变量捕获：** tialaramex指出在C++中可以通过使用std::shared_ptr等方式控制变量的生命周期，但有经验的C++程序员通常不会这么做，因为容易导致引用超过其所指对象生命周期的问题。C++允许程序员选择如何处理这些情况，但很容易出错并在运行时引发问题。

• **Rust中的安全机制：** tialaramex对比了Rust和C++，强调Rust的编译器会在编译时指出潜在问题，从而避免运行时错误。Rust提供了如`move`关键字和`Rc`类型等工具来安全地处理变量捕获和共享引用。

• **Lisp中的回调与查询：** thesz分享了Lisp中的一个实际用例，其中闭包和回调用于收集各种项目，并指出简单的SQL样查询可以实现类似功能。thesz还提到对Tcl作为多范式编程语言的兴趣，并分享了关于代数类型的实现。

• **Tcl的现状与社区：** gitroom对Tcl仍有活跃的社区表示惊讶，而dingnuts则询问Tcl是否正在复兴以及其社区的聚集地。

补充讨论：
• **闭包的实际应用：** RHSeeger提出了闭包可以用于返回一组操作同一组变量的方法，即对象的行为。这表明闭包在实现某些设计模式时非常有用。

• **多范式语言的潜力：** thesz对Tcl作为多范式语言的能力表示认可，并通过分享具体的编程模式（如代数类型）展示了Tcl的灵活性。

争议焦点：
• **C++的复杂性与安全性：** C++提供了灵活的变量捕获方式，但这种灵活性也带来了容易出错的风险。相比之下，Rust通过编译时检查来提高安全性，但其实现可能更加复杂。

data.title: Speedrunning and Modding the Incredibles: Rise of the Underminer
data.author: farlow
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了对《The Incredibles: Rise of the Underminer》这款游戏进行逆向工程和修改（modding）以优化速通（speedrun）的过程。作者解释了为何过去的作弊码书籍和网站提供的作弊码不完整或不准确，并展示了游戏的调试功能和一些出界漏洞（glitches）。

作者通过静态逆向工程分析游戏的战斗系统，使用Ghidra工具分析GameCube游戏的可执行文件（.dol），并幸运地发现游戏包含调试符号，使得函数名称可读。然而，直接从代码中寻找可利用的战斗行为较为困难。

为了更好地实验和反馈，作者决定制作一个显示所有敌人生命值的mod。通过建立C工具链，修改游戏并在Dolphin模拟器中使用Action Replay作弊码实现。最终，作者发现了一些战斗系统的细节，例如连续拳击伤害加倍的现象，从而为速通提供了优化策略。

通过这些方法，作者成功地优化了游戏速通，并展示了具体的效果和数据。

optimize a speedrun. On the way, I’ll answer why cheat code books (remember

game. I’ll also show some of the game’s debug features and a couple out of

. At the time, the
casual run was fast enough for the
WR in the Co-Op Glitchless
category
at 1:04:58.
Someone beat us just a short while later. We haven’t been able to beat it since.
It’s time to get serious, so let’s reverse engineer the game to look for
optimizations.
The whole point of rotu is to beat up robots as you progress through 11 levels.
The game ends with a boss fight against
The
Underminer
, the villain
introduced at the end of the first Incredibles film.
Since so much of the game is combat focused, if we can figure out how to
optimize combat, we can shave time off our run.
Reverse Engineering
One way we can learn about the combat system is to statically reverse engineer
the game. A Gamecube iso will include a .dol file, which is the
executable file
format for the GameCube
. We can use
Cuyler36’s
Ghidra-GameCube-Loader
to
load the .dol file into
Ghidra
. This will allow us to see the PowerPC
instructions along with Ghidra’s attempted C decompilation.
We’re very lucky that rotu is one of
~10% of GameCube games that shipped with
debug symbols
. This
means that we’re able to read function names. Here’s an arbitrary example of the
kind of decompilation we’re working with:
/* __thiscall zNPC::zNPCBomber::GetCombatData(void) */
undefined
**
__thiscall
zNPC
::
zNPCBomber
::

(

*
this
)
{
int
iVar1
;

;

=
(

(
code
**
)(
*

)(
this
+
0xdc
)
+
0x100
))();
ppuVar2
=
&
@

@
zNPCBomber_cpp

::
bomberEliteCombatInitData
;

(

There’s a lot of code defining the combat system, and it’s not obvious where we
should start looking. It seems hard to find interesting or exploitable combat
behavior by just reading the code, since there are a lot of interacting
components and the emergent behavior is hard to reason about.
Modding
I realized that what I actually wanted was a mod that will draw the health of all
the enemies on the screen. That way, we can experiment with ideas in-game and
get immediate feedback on the effect on the enemy’s health.
The idea is simple in theory. First, we’ll look at Ghidra to find where enemies
are stored in memory. We’ll also find useful functions we can call, like a text
rendering function. Then, we’ll insert a hook into the main render function and
draw text on the screen at the entities’ projected screen coordinates.
To do this in practice, we’ll first set up a
C
toolchain
so we can
write mods in C against the actual rotu game engine. The toolchain first
compiles C to PowerPC via
DevkitPPC
. Then
it parses the game’s .dol file to determine which patches to write where, and
finally it outputs an Action Replay code that will write the compiled
instructions of the mod to the right places.
All that’s left is to write
the
mod
! It’s ergonomic
to be able to leverage existing functions in the game engine, like libc
functions, but more importantly, we can use functions that draw textboxes and
convert world coordinates to screen coordinates.
Action Replay
As mentioned above, the final output of the toolchain is an
Action
Replay
code. The Action Replay is
a game cheating device that the
Dolphin emulator
also supports. I chose to use Action Replay codes instead of patching the game
because they’re easy to share and it makes for a good story. The best docs for
GameCube AR codes are on the
Dolphin GitHub
wiki
.
In an Action Replay code, each line is an instruction. As I understand, these
instructions get executed ~every frame. For our purposes, we’ll only make use of
the “write memory” instructions to write our mod’s instructions where they need
to go. This works fine in an emulator. No idea if it works on real hardware.
You can see the final AR code
here
. It’s
hilarious long: 1.2k lines long at the time of this writing!
Results
Check out the mod in action!
An example subtle observation that is made possible with this method is that
Frozone’s ice glide does different damage depending on how long he is in contact
with the enemy. It’s as if it can “hit twice”:
Perhaps the most important observation is just that punching is overpowered. In
particular, the punch damage doubles for sequential punches, up to 4 punches.

43878191.article_summary:
本文介绍了对《The Incredibles: Rise of the Underminer》这款游戏进行逆向工程和修改（modding）以优化速通（speedrun）的过程。作者解释了为何过去的作弊码书籍和网站提供的作弊码不完整或不准确，并展示了游戏的调试功能和一些出界漏洞（glitches）。

作者通过静态逆向工程分析游戏的战斗系统，使用Ghidra工具分析GameCube游戏的可执行文件（.dol），并幸运地发现游戏包含调试符号，使得函数名称可读。然而，直接从代码中寻找可利用的战斗行为较为困难。

为了更好地实验和反馈，作者决定制作一个显示所有敌人生命值的mod。通过建立C工具链，修改游戏并在Dolphin模拟器中使用Action Replay作弊码实现。最终，作者发现了一些战斗系统的细节，例如连续拳击伤害加倍的现象，从而为速通提供了优化策略。

通过这些方法，作者成功地优化了游戏速通，并展示了具体的效果和数据。

data.title: A memory of the nineteen nineties (1997)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了叙述者在1997年6月3日下午两点十分，于伦敦大英博物馆圆形阅览室内等待一个消失多年的人——Enoch Soames——的归来。Soames是一位寂寂无名的诗人，生前与魔鬼达成交易，被送往未来以确认自己在文学史上的地位。然而，他在1997年的图书馆目录中发现，自己仅被视为Max Beerbohm故事中的虚构人物。最终，Soames被魔鬼带走，从此再未出现。叙述者为了见证这一时刻，特地长途跋涉来到此地，呼应了Soames当年消失与归来的传说。文章通过叙述者对往事和Soames故事的回顾，营造了一种神秘与宿命交织的氛围。

Return to the
Table of Contents.
N O V E M B E R  1 9 9 7
Being a faithful account of the events of the designated day, when the man who had disappeared was expected briefly to return
by
Teller
O
NE FORTY-NINE P.M. The gilded clock that looks down on the Round Reading Room
at the British Museum has no second hand. But I am watching very closely. I can
actually see the minute hand creeping toward the Roman numeral X.
Discuss this article in the
Arts & Literature
forum of
Post &
Riposte.
Above, the vast blue plaster dome with its arched windows and skylight is
just as it was a hundred years ago, on that terrible day when --
A distant loose-leaf binder clicks shut.
It's 1:53. Soon it will be two o'clock. Then, at last, 2:10, the moment I have
been waiting for. To be here, in this spot in London, on this day at ten past
two, I have traveled 4,000 miles and planned for thirty-four and a half
years.
*  *  *
Thirty-four and a half years ago I was  sitting in a nearly empty high school
classroom in Philadelphia under the spell of my English teacher and drama
coach, D. G. Rosenbaum. I idolized Mr. Rosenbaum (or "Rosey," as we Drama
Society brats called him). He had a dark, resonant voice. He had a widow's peak
and a moustache and goatee that made him look like Mephistopheles; he hinted
that his ancestors were Scottish warlocks. He wore trim black suits, blood-red
vests, and pince-nez. He smoked black cigarettes with gold tips, and made them
vanish by sleight of hand when the principal was nearby. Rosey knew
psychoanalysis. He quoted Aristotle, Kenneth Burke, and Ezra Pound in everyday
conversation. He ordered his milkshakes spiked with raw eggs.
That afternoon Rosey was entertaining half a dozen aspiring young actors by
reading aloud "Enoch Soames: A Memory of the Eighteen-Nineties," by Max
Beerbohm. "Soames" is a sharp sketch of a dull poet Beerbohm encountered in
London just before the turn of the century.
He was a stooping, shambling person, rather tall, very pale, with longish and
brownish hair. He had a thin vague beard -- or rather, he had a chin on which a
large number of hairs weakly curled and clustered to cover its retreat....
The young writers of that era -- and I was sure this man was a writer -- strove
earnestly to be distinct in aspect. This man had striven unsuccessfully. He
wore a soft black hat of clerical kind but of Bohemian intention, and a grey
waterproof cape which, perhaps because it was waterproof, failed to be
romantic. I decided that "dim" was the
mot juste
for him.
Soames's poems were equally dim. His most successful book sold only three
copies. But his vanity was untarnished. Soames was certain that future
generations would recognize his genius.
On the afternoon of June 3, 1897, Beerbohm was talking with Soames in a Soho
café when a sinister stranger in a scarlet vest interrupted. The
stranger introduced himself as the Devil and made an offer. He would transport
Soames a hundred years into the future, to visit the Round Reading Room of the
British Museum
as it would be in 1997.
Here Soames could consult the
library's all-knowing catalogue and at last be sure of his place in literary
history. The price for such a trip: eternity in Hell. Soames accepted. At ten
past two on June 3, 1897, Enoch Soames vanished into the future.
Later that afternoon Soames reappeared in the little café. He looked
grim and immediately got drunk. Beerbohm prodded him to recount his trip.
Soames said that his arrival in the Reading Room of 1997 had caused a sensation.
"They stared at
me,
I can tell you.... I think I rather scared
them. They moved away whenever I came near. They followed me about at a
distance, wherever I went. The men at the round desk in the middle seemed to
have a sort of panic...."
Soames had gone straight to the catalogue and had taken out the volume he hoped
would contain endless editions, critiques, and annotations of his work. He
found none. He searched the library all afternoon, until at last he found one
lone mention of his name in a book on English literature of the late nineteenth
century.
Enoch Soames, the book said, was an
imaginary character in a story by Max
Beerbohm.
Just as Soames finished telling Beerbohm about his visit to 1997, the
Rosey-esque stranger reappeared and dragged the poor poet away, presumably to
Hell. He was never seen again. But, Beerbohm wrote,
You realise that the reading-room into which Soames was projected by the Devil
was in all respects precisely as it will be on the afternoon of June 3, 1997.
You realise, therefore, that on that afternoon, when it comes round, there the
self-same crowd will be, and there Soames too will be, punctually....
The fact that people are going to stare at him, and follow him around, and seem
afraid of him, can be explained only on the hypothesis that they will somehow
have been prepared for his ghostly visitation....

data.title: What New Orleans Taught Me
data.author: tintinnabula
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者在新奥尔良生活十年后，难以离开这座城市的情感与体会。每年茉莉花开时，新奥尔良的独特节奏让离开变得尤为困难。作者通过与邻居的闲谈、城市的缓慢节奏以及多任务处理的文化，学会了如何在这里生活。新奥尔良的时间观念是循环且关系性的，这与美国其他地方的线性时间观不同。在这里，作者体验了便宜的房租、独特的酒吧文化和丰富的夜生活，感受到城市既慢又快的独特节奏。

此外，作者还通过在路易斯安那的沼泽中划皮艇和听自然声音，领悟到这座城市需要耐心去倾听和体会。在社会关怀方面，作者反思了左右派在道德关怀范围上的差异，并从新奥尔良的社区活动中找到了平衡普遍关怀与个人关怀的模式。最终，经过十年，作者觉得自己已经学到了这座城市要教给他的东西，现在是离开的时候了。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新奥尔良（NOLA）的城市文化、科技社区、生活质量以及其独特性与存在的问题

不同观点：
• **新奥尔良的科技社区正在发展**：bhelx认为新奥尔良有一个活跃的小型科技社区，并提供了一个相关活动的链接，表示愿意为感兴趣的人引荐。
• **新奥尔良的独特魅力与安全隐患并存**：julienchastang欣赏新奥尔良的“ grit ”（粗粝感），包括美食和现场音乐，尤其是Frenchman街的音乐表演，但同时也提到安全隐患，特别是在夜晚的法国区（French Quarter）。
• **生活成本低但问题不少**：b8指出新奥尔良的科技机会不多，很多人生活在贫困中，政治腐败，公共学校关闭，洪水和犯罪率高。然而，生活成本低和美食是吸引他回到这里的原因。
• **不同城区的独特氛围**：catapps将新奥尔良的不同城区与美国其他地区进行比较，认为每个区域都有其独特的氛围，使得整个城市非常特别。

43864442.article_content:
It’s hard to leave
New Orleans when the jasmine is in bloom — especially when you’ve spent a decade learning its rhythm. The scent floats in the air like a soft spell, the sudden sweetness a harbinger of spring and the slow turning of seasons. The white flowers seem to appear all at once, adorning the tangled vines that trace the city’s fences and phone poles.
A friend tells me that every city you live in is a kind of love affair. Some are short and tempestuous, others stretch across seasons, years. After 10 years with New Orleans, I finally know it is time to go. They say it takes exactly as long to move as you need it to. I think I needed that whole time to learn what this place was trying to teach me — about pace, about care, and about feeling things in your bones.
PACE
My first home was a house in the Irish Channel, a red camelback shotgun with too many roommates and not enough hallways. What I remember most are my neighbors sitting on their porches every day, long talks interrupted only by the sounds of Mr. Okra driving through the streets selling vegetables. Compared with what I knew from the East Coast, the most striking difference was the pace of things. People just seemed to have more time, and a willingness to spend it on others.
Years later I would learn a word for this ,  that New Orleans has aspects of a polychronic society, in contrast to the more rigid monochronic frame that dominates the rest of the country. In polychronic cultures, time is seen as cyclical and relational rather than fixed. That shift in orientation touches everything: multitasking, unscheduled connection, a generosity of presence. Much of what’s good about New Orleans ,  from its rhythms to its spices ,  comes from Latin America and Africa. So, too, does its relationship to time.
Everyone thinks their early 20s were the golden age of the place they lived, but New Orleans in 2015–2020 had a special quality to it. Cheap rent. The best dive bars in the world. DJ Soul Sister spinning classic vinyl Saturday’s at Hi Ho Lounge. The Superdome rocking with Drew Brees. Somehow, it felt like there was time to do it all. For my 20s, New Orleans was the Goldilocks city — slow enough to feel luxurious, fast enough never to bore you, big enough to feel expansive, small enough to always run into someone at the grocery store.
When people ask me about Louisiana, I often start by talking about the swamp. I tell them there’s more life in a cubic inch of swamp muck than in a whole pile of Virginia clay. But you have to know what to look for. The swamp doesn’t offer the postcard peaks of the Sierras or the expansive plains and skies of West Texas. It reveals itself slowly, paddle by paddle.
One night during a kayaking trip in the Ponchatoula Basin, I lay in a hammock strung up between old cypress trees. Dusk came with a deafening chorus of frogs, the clicking of katydids, the rustle of roosting herons. That night I happened to be awake at 2:00 am and heard the heavy splash of an alligator rolling off of a log. Louisiana can’t just be seen ;  it has to be heard. The choice is deciding to stick around long enough to listen.
CARE
One feature of being alive for the last decade is that we’ve had lots of time to soul search about why things are on the wrong track, and how our society has become so polarized.
Recently, a heatmap from a 2019 study in
Nature
called “
Ideological Differences in the Expanse of the Moral Circle
” made the rounds on the internet. Participants were asked to assign moral concern to various groups of people. The allocation options began with immediate family and radiated outward to “all things in existence.” The heatmaps could not be more different across political divides: liberal respondents’ allocation was clustered at the outer edge, toward the universal; conservatives were more concentrated on their inner circles.
Each side interpreted the findings to confirm what they already believed. Liberals scorned conservatives’ narrow empathy ,  demonstrated in their recent glee over the dismantling of foreign aid and unlawful detentions. After all, what kind of life is it to lead where you can’t extend your care beyond just your family and friends?
On the other hand, conservatives mocked liberals for caring more about “all natural things in the universe, including rocks” than about their grandmothers. On its face, the criticism is unfair (last I checked, grandmothers are included in “all natural things”!), but the thread is worth pulling, reflecting arguments from progressive movement leaders about how internal dynamics are harming our movements for social change (adrienne marie brown & Maurice Mitchell, to name a few). I know from my own experience that it is true: sometimes we are so focused on the universal that we forget to inhabit a lived politics of care.
In New Orleans, I found a model for balancing these perspectives. I’ll never forget my first second line, a massive parade snowballing through the Treme and snarling traffic

此外，作者还通过在路易斯安那的沼泽中划皮艇和听自然声音，领悟到这座城市需要耐心去倾听和体会。在社会关怀方面，作者反思了左右派在道德关怀范围上的差异，并从新奥尔良的社区活动中找到了平衡普遍关怀与个人关怀的模式。最终，经过十年，作者觉得自己已经学到了这座城市要教给他的东西，现在是离开的时候了。

data.article_summary: QModem 4.51是20世纪80年代至90年代初运行的MS-DOS电信程序，由John Friel III开发。该源码版本为1992年初的“试用版”，供电信爱好者及复古计算爱好者参考。QModem支持多种调制解调器协议、脚本、自定义配置、自动调制解调器配置，甚至包含一个简易BBS主机模式。其功能包括全屏拨号目录、丰富的脚本支持、ANSI等终端仿真、滚动缓冲区、鼠标支持等。源码使用Turbo Pascal和x86汇编编写，包含完整的构建文件和工具。由于其历史性，在现代环境中构建需要适应和实验。

QModem 4.51 Source Code
The source code release of
QModem 4.51
, an MS-DOS telecommunications program authored by John Friel III (1960–2024). This source snapshot reflects the state of QModem "Test-Drive" edition, version 4.51, as it existed in early 1992. The release is presented in the hope it may prove valuable as a historical artifact, for telecommunications enthusiasts, retrocomputing hobbyists, or anyone interested in the inner workings of a classic DOS comms package.
QModem was a widely-used terminal communications program for MS-DOS, supporting a rich array of modem protocols, scripting, user customization, modem auto-configuration, and even a "Host Mode" for basic BBS-like operation.
Historical Overview
QModem
was developed throughout the 1980s and early 1990s as a competitor to programs such as Procomm, Telix, and others. It provided robust support for:
Many modem speeds and hardware types (8250, 16450, 16550 UARTs, and special hardware)
Internal and external file transfer protocols: XMODEM, YMODEM, ZMODEM, and user-defined protocol support via external drivers
Full-screen dialing directory (the
.FON
phonebook)
Extensive scripting and automation via its built-in script language
In-program configuration via a full-featured setup menu (
Alt-N
)
ANSI/VT100/TTY/Avatar terminal emulations
Host Mode: a mini BBS server included in the client!
Scrollback buffer, split screen terminal
Mouse support, custom keyboard macros, and more
File Layout and Project Structure
This repository contains the complete Turbo Pascal source code, as well as supporting assembler, batch, and utility files.
Main Directories and Files
.PAS
— Turbo Pascal source files implementing the main program, modules, and utilities
.ASM
— x86 assembler routines for performance-critical sections and hardware interfacing
.BAT
— DOS batch files for building, testing, and packaging
.OBJ, .INC
— Included binaries and Pascal include files
.KEY, .FON, .CNF, etc.
— Sample data, key, configuration, or phonebook files
Significant modules include:
QMODEM.PAS
— Main entry point
QMMAIN.PAS
— Main application logic
INITIAL.PAS
— Global configuration, terminal, and comm settings
COMM.PAS
/
COMM2.PAS
— Serial communications support
DOWNLD*.PAS
/
UPLD*.PAS
— File transfer protocol implementations
TP*
,
OP*
— Support code, likely Turbo Professional or custom libraries
HOST.PAS
— Host Mode/BBS functionality
FONESTUF.PAS
,
QDIAL.PAS
, etc. — Dialing directory and phonebook features
SCRIPTS*.PAS
— Script engine and automation
INSTALL*.PAS
,
QINSTALL.PAS
,
RUNQINST.PAS
— On-disk configuration and setup utility
Building QModem
This is a historical codebase.
QModem 4.51 targets MS-DOS using Turbo Pascal 5.x/6.0, with Turbo Professional and potentially other Borland or third-party libraries.
Potential Build Approaches
Turbo Pascal 5.5/6.0
(MS-DOS or DOSBox): This is almost certainly the original toolchain. If you have a copy, opening
QMODEM.PAS
as the project and compiling (after possibly setting appropriate memory and overlay paths) may work. Some makefiles or batch files, e.g.
BUILD.BAT
, may be helpful, but will need adaptation to your environment.
TP/BP Emulation or Cross-Compilers
:
Free Pascal
includes some support for Turbo Pascal compatibility, but differences are likely extensive (including use of inline assembler, overlays, and third-party libraries).
Turbo Professional & Dependencies
: Many of the
TP*
units (e.g.
TpDos
,
TpCrt
, etc.) are from the
Turbo Professional library
. You'll need the corresponding TPUs and sources for your compiler version.
Manual Assembly of .ASM Files
: Assembler files need to be assembled (e.g. with TURBO assembler or MASM) and linked or compiled as .OBJ for use with Turbo Pascal.
Overlay Management
: Note the project extensively uses Borland/Turbo Pascal overlays (
.OVR
files, see
OVR01.INC
and overlay units). Disk layout and path settings for overlays must be matched as the original program expects.
Build Scripts
Several build-automation batch files are included, such as:
BUILD.BAT
BUILDOVR.BAT
BUG.BAT
DEBUGOVR.BAT
Inspect and adapt these scripts as necessary for your own environment.
Modernization Caveats
No supported modern environment
targets this code directly. Efforts to port or run on anything but MS-DOS/Turbo Pascal 5.x/6.x are purely experimental and will require code and/or dependency adaptation.
Third-party libraries
(Turbo Professional, OpKey, possibly others) are required.
Hardware-dependence
: Much code assumes direct access to PC hardware, BIOS, and serial port inte

data.title: Run LLMs on Apple Neural Engine (ANE)
data.author: behnamoh
data.article_summary: ANEMLL是一个开源项目，旨在加速大型语言模型（LLM）向张量处理器的移植，最初专注于苹果神经引擎（ANE）。其目标是提供从模型转换到推理的完整开源管道，支持常见LLM架构在ANE上的设备端推理，适用于低功耗的边缘设备，确保隐私和安全。主要组件包括LLM转换工具、Swift参考实现、核心推理引擎、Python示例代码和iOS/macOS示例应用。当前的0.3.0 Alpha版本支持从Hugging Face模型转换为CoreML格式，主要支持LLAMA 3.1等模型，未来将支持更多模型。项目提供了示例应用和模型下载，并包含性能测试工具。用户可以通过Swift CLI运行模型，并使用TestFlight测试iOS/macOS应用。

不同观点：
• **behnamoh** 提到 Apple 的 ANE 优化模型声称性能大幅提升，但现有的工具如 MLX 和 llama.cpp 不支持 ANE。虽然 llama.cpp 开始探索支持 ANE，但 MLX 由于封闭的 API 无法支持 ANE。
• **cowmix** 分享了 Qualcomm 类似的宣传，指出尽管声称 NPU 可以处理大语言模型（LLM），但实际运行中仍以 CPU 为主，且 NPU 仅对小模型有功率效率优势，对大模型表现不佳，GPU 也不理想。
• **sunpazed** 通过实测指出 ANE 在功耗上的优势（如 M1 Max 和 M4 Pro 的对比），但 ANE 模型的上下文限制为 512 个 tokens，生产环境使用受限。
• **htk** 认为 ANE 是浪费的硅片空间，建议增加更多 GPU 核心，并通过 GPU 处理神经网络任务。
• **antirez** 认为关键在于性能提升的量化数据，是否值得从现有平台切换。
• **simonw** 试图找出 Apple 的技术核心，认为 Core ML 工具可能是关键，或是否有其他重要技术。
• **daedrdev** 强调 Apple 统一内存架构的优势，可以运行更大模型，而无需多个 GPU。
• **jvstokes** 提问 Core ML 是否利用了 ANE，是否存在需要更低层级访问的瓶颈。
• **cwoolfe** 关注 M 系列 MacBook 上 ANE 的推理速度是否有性能优势，或者只是为了在 iOS 等平台上运行。
• **gitroom** 批评 Apple 对 ANE 的严格控制，质疑这种做法是为了保持控制，还是技术原因。
• **kamranjon** 询问 Apple 硅片中的神经核心是否对训练有用，或仅限于推理，如 whisper.cpp 使用了这些核心。
• **randmeerkat** 讽刺 Siri 的智能表现不佳，暗示尽管有先进硬件，软件层面仍有问题。
• **neves** 询问 Microsoft Copilot AI 笔记本是否能快速运行有用的模型。
• **m3kw9** 指出即使是 1GB 模型对手机来说也太大了，难以实现大众化应用。

补充讨论：
• ANE 优化的实际性能提升和应用场景受限问题。
• 不同硬件（如 NPU、GPU、CPU）在处理 LLM 上的表现对比。
• Apple 对 ANE 的封闭策略引发的争议与用户 frustration。
• 对 ML 模型在不同平台（iOS、Mac、Qualcomm 设备）上运行的实际需求与技术挑战。

ANEMLL
ANEMLL (pronounced like "animal") is an open-source project focused on accelerating the porting of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tensor processors, starting with the Apple Neural Engine (ANE).
Goals
The goal is to provide a fully open-source pipeline from model conversion to inference for common LLM architectures running on ANE.
This enables seamless integration and on-device inference for low-power applications on edge devices, ensuring maximum privacy and security.
This is critical for autonomous applications, where models run directly on the device without requiring an internet connection.
We aim to:
Provide flexible and easy to use library/framework to port LLMs to ANE directly from Hugging Face models
Provide on-device examples for iOS and macOS swift or C/C++ Applications
See update
Roadmap.md
for more details
Main Components in 0.3.0 Alpha Release
ANEMLL provides five main components for Apple Neural Engine inference development:
LLM Conversion Tools
- Scripts and code to convert models directly from Hugging Face weights

Swift Reference Implementation

anemll-swift-cli

43879702.article_summary: ANEMLL是一个开源项目，旨在加速大型语言模型（LLM）向张量处理器的移植，最初专注于苹果神经引擎（ANE）。其目标是提供从模型转换到推理的完整开源管道，支持常见LLM架构在ANE上的设备端推理，适用于低功耗的边缘设备，确保隐私和安全。主要组件包括LLM转换工具、Swift参考实现、核心推理引擎、Python示例代码和iOS/macOS示例应用。当前的0.3.0 Alpha版本支持从Hugging Face模型转换为CoreML格式，主要支持LLAMA 3.1等模型，未来将支持更多模型。项目提供了示例应用和模型下载，并包含性能测试工具。用户可以通过Swift CLI运行模型，并使用TestFlight测试iOS/macOS应用。

data.article_summary: 文章探讨了在当今低质量内容泛滥的时代，精湛的技艺（craft）如何成为一种反抗。作者通过与独立游戏工匠Neal Agarwal的对话，讨论了技艺、编程及创作自由的重要性。Neal是知名网站Neal.fun的创始人，以创作古怪、有趣且病毒式传播的游戏闻名。他自十岁起开始制作游戏，使用Microsoft Frontpage创建了第一个网站，并在Scratch平台上开始编程。他在高中时制作了数据可视化网站everysecond.io，并逐渐发展出自己的创作风格。Neal强调了在独立创作中保持艺术自由和创作活力的重要性，他的经历展示了在当今"低质化"网络环境中，坚持高品质创作的独特价值。文章还涉及AI崛起、LLM（大语言模型）对创作的影响等话题。

A while back, I
said
I’d be experimenting with new ways to share what I’m thinking about, what I’m tinkering with, and conversations I’m having.
I’ve also been thinking a lot about what makes creation meaningful, and I’ve landed on a timely thesis:
In the age of slop, craft is rebellion.
This series,
The Craft
, is a multi-format experiment I’m hosting here, all about the art of making things, and what makes the maker, too.
I recently grabbed coffee with
Neal Agarwal
, the indie game artisan behind
Neal.fun
, a cult-favorite corner of the internet home to
weird
,
delightful
, wildly viral games like
The Password Game
and
Infinite Craft
.
Neal is a quiet legend in the indie game world. He’s made the web his canvas for playable art and joyful mischief — a kind of one-man artisanal rebellion against the slopification of everything. I’ve long admired how he’s carved a beloved niche, stayed independent, profitable, and rooted in craft — all while reaching millions.
We covered
a lot
— and Neal asked me a few questions too.
Some hot topics from our conversation:
Making 100 games before turning 20
His one and only job — at MSCHF
Why he went indie to build Neal.fun
The rise of AI and “vibe coding”
How LLMs powered
Infinite Craft
Viral hits and artistic freedom
Staying creatively energized (for years)
Extended Cut: favorite games, the slopification of everything, LLMs for writing, chatbot kids, new religion, & more.
This conversation has been edited & condensed for clarity. (P.S. No LLMs were used in the placement of em dashes.)
A terminally online playground.
“I made my first website when I was 10. From 10 to 20, I probably made 100 games.”
Neal’s
first game
Let’s talk about the beginnings of what many people know you for:
games
. When did you first start making games, and how?
I was very terminally online as a kid. Most of my friends were online too. So I just got sucked into different forums centered around making games.
I made my first website when I was about 10 using
Microsoft Frontpage
, it was a collection of links to my favorite flash games I played in school. I started making my own games when I found
Scratch
, and that was my first real foray into programming and making something and putting it out into the world.
The first game I ever made was based on the British TV show
Wipeout
. It was a platformer where each level was an obstacle course. The game is actually still up
here
! I love that kids are still commenting on it (“this is a great game! But what would make it even better is the OG
Wipeout
music.”)
How many games do you think you made in that 10-year span?
They were all really small games, and not that great, but probably about 100.
That’s a lot! Did those early games show enough promise or give you some other sign to keep making games?
They did, it felt really good having people play my games even if it was just other 12-year olds. I also spent more time learning how to make websites. Pretty quickly I realized that I wanted my own home on the internet.
As a teenager I started getting really into data visualizations. I made one called
everysecond.io
, which tracked how many iPhones, iPads, etc. Apple sold. It was my first website to gain some traction. A couple media outlets wrote about it, and I remember thinking,
“Oh, that’s cool.”
In high school, I made another site called
kamogo.com
, a mix between
XKCD
and the stuff I do now. I called them interactive comics because the jokes were in the UI interactions.
Looking back, it was the same ethos as
The Password Game
: the UI itself as a medium for telling jokes. There were lots of other blogs/comic sites I loved, like
The Oatmeal
and
Wait But Why
. I spent most of school daydreaming about side projects. I knew I wanted to be making stuff on the web.
The origin story of
Neal.fun
.
“My parents were like, you’ve got to stop buying these domains because it’s adding up every year. So, I bought Neal.fun and decided to just put everything there.”
Neal’s
catalog
of web games, count: 34
You studied computer science in college — did it help at all, or were you already capable and set on building your own things?
Studying computer science in college isn’t a very creative endeavor. So it helped in the sense that I disliked college so much that I needed to go soul searching. Sophomore year I was at a pretty low point. Programming had been my escape, but in college I started falling out of love with it because now it was school work. I felt like now I didn’t even have that to fall back on. I felt an overwhelming urge to create

data.title: How LWN is faring in 2025
data.author: leephillips
data.article_summary: 2025年，LWN面临订阅量下降的挑战，主要由于美国经济波动和全球贸易紧张局势。虽然这不至于威胁LWN的生存，但仍令人担忧。为了应对，LWN在控制成本的同时，继续提供高质量的Linux和自由软件社区报道。通胀导致订阅收入购买力下降，但目前没有涨价计划。未来，若情况恶化，可能不得不涨价。LWN感谢长期读者的支持，呼吁新读者订阅，并建议现有订阅者升级以帮助LWN度过经济难关。多位读者表示愿意支付更高费用以支持LWN的持续运营。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LWN（Linux Weekly News）的可持续性及相关经济环境影响的讨论

不同观点：
• ofrzeta认为，LWN这样的出版物必须不惜一切代价维持下去，他建议通过捐赠或订阅来支持其运营。
• wood_spirit持不同意见，指出由于经济原因，许多人（包括潜在的LWN订阅者）正在缩减可自由支配的开支，暗示LWN可能也会受到影响。
• markvdb则建议通过让雇主订阅团体订阅来支持LWN，强调这对于从事自由/开源软件的人是一个不错的选择。

补充讨论：
• vlovich123关注全球贸易问题，特别是国际支付可能受到的影响，并提出通过设立子公司来绕过支付障碍的可能性。
• qwe----3对LWN能够支付高额薪水表示质疑，特别提到支付给Linus 150万美元年薪的问题，暗示对LWN财务状况的怀疑。
• nu11ptr试图将LWN面临的困境与更广泛的经济背景联系起来，询问这是否与对美国的反对情绪或即将到来的经济衰退有关。
• jgalt212则反驳有关市场下行的观点，引用Barrons的文章指出市场实际上在上涨，表明经济状况并不像其他人说的那样悲观。

争议焦点：
• LWN是否能在当前经济环境下继续生存，特别是在许多人削减开支的情况下。
• 国际贸易和支付问题是否会严重影响LWN的运营。
• LWN的财务健康状况，尤其是高额薪水支出的合理性。
• 当前经济环境是否真的不利，以及这是否会影响LWN的订阅和支持。

总结：讨论的核心在于LWN的可持续性及其在当前经济环境下面临的挑战，包括订阅者财务状况、国际支付问题以及更广泛的经济因素的影响。

How LWN is faring in 2025
[Posted April 30, 2025 by corbet]
Just over six months ago, The Economist described the US economy as "
the envy of the
world
".  That headline would be unlikely to appear now.  The economic
boom referenced in that article feels like a distant memory, markets are
falling, and uncertainty is at an all-time high.  Like everybody else, LWN
is affected by the current turbulence in the political and economic
spheres; we expect to get through this period, but there will be some
challenges.
To put it bluntly: starting around the beginning of March, we have observed
a distinct drop in both new subscriptions and renewals.  That timing
roughly corresponds with the US administration's increasing attacks on the
global system of trade and the economic downturn that has been its result.
As it stands, this subscription drop does not pose an existential threat to
LWN — or to the salaries of its writers — but it is a matter of concern.
We are responding by tightening our belt where we can, but otherwise
working to provide the best coverage of the Linux and free-software
communities, as we always have.  Readers can help, of course, by
subscribing
if they have not already done so.
Encouraging your employer to set up a
group subscription
is especially
helpful.  Subscriptions are the only thing that has kept LWN operating for
all these years.
Beyond the immediate situation, there are a number of potential problems to
be concerned about.  For example, inflation did not stop after our price
increase in 2022, with the result that subscription dollars buy
significantly less then they once did.  We are
not
considering a
price increase at this time but, if the situation worsens, we may have to
go there.
For better or worse, LWN is a US-based company, but a large portion of
our subscription sales come from outside the country.  If the backlash
against US companies grows, we are unlikely to escape its effects entirely.
Further attacks on global trade could make it more difficult for us to
accept payments from outside the country, even when the buyer is willing.
In a truly terrible world, there may be attempts to reduce US participation
in (and support for) free software; the probability of that seems low, but
not zero.
Those are all future worries, though. For now, we will focus on getting
through the current economic storms.  The good news is that LWN has been
here since 1998, which is long enough to have been through more than one
difficult cycle.  We are still here, thanks entirely to the steady support
from you, our readers.  Our subscribers, especially, have our gratitude; if
you have not yet subscribed to LWN, please consider doing so now.
Meanwhile our primary focus will remain being worthy of the support you all
have given us since the beginning.  It is the least we can do for all of
you who have made our existence possible for the last 27 years.
